repository.whyPublic: electron-updater reads latest.yml from the release page with no credentials; a private repo would mean compiling a GitHub token into every copy of the app.

workflow.releasePolicy: Standing instruction (2026-09-27, replaces 2026-09-07): release ONLY when the owner says "push". Until then: make the changes, unit tests for what was touched, npm run pack:test, report. On "push": Electron check (npm run check:browsers), all tests, fixes, then npm run push - GitHub, nebula-web, the flash, every MD file. Never ask which platforms to build: the repo is public, Actions is free on both runners.

quality.smokeCommand: npm run build && npm run smoke

invariants: The dev app and the installed app never share a profile — npm run dev sets NEBULA_USER_DATA to <repo>/.dev-profile.
Sample notes are seeded only when the vault was read successfully AND came back empty. An unreadable vault disables the disk mirror instead.
The Windows in-app installer copies the vault to backups/pre-update-<version>-<time>. Manual Mac and portable replacement does not invoke this hook; take a closed-profile backup first.
electron-updater stays in dependencies and external in vite.config.js; CI asserts both latest.yml and its presence in the asar.
win.signAndEditExecutable must stay unset — false also disables rcedit, which is what writes the exe's icon and version info.
The `hidden` attribute is only a UA display:none - any author `display` rule beats it. app.css carries [hidden]{display:none!important}; assert computed display in tests, never el.hidden.
Shapes live on two layers (.shape-layer and .shape-layer--behind). 'Send behind text' moves the node between them; a class alone cannot cross a stacking context.
npm run kill closes Nebula.exe, Nebula Test.exe and the versioned portable; pack:test runs it first, so the test build refreshes without anyone closing a window.

Every build seeds the SAME single guide note. Seeding still only happens on an empty, successfully-read vault; NoteStore.ensureGuide adds the guide to an older vault once per GUIDE_VERSION, adding only - never editing or deleting.
Note colours are CLASSES (c-*, h-*) resolved per theme in tokens.css, never hex written into the note - three themes make any frozen value unreadable on two of them. A highlight forces its own ink.
Never hide an Electron <webview> with hidden/display:none: the guest is detached and reloads, losing the session. Stack the views and switch visibility (.ai-view).

Scripted edits to note content must go through a real edit command (insertHTML, styleWithCSS+fontName). Replacing an element execCommand just inserted breaks Chromium's undo stack and Ctrl+Z leaves duplicated text.
Searching never marks up the note: find.js paints ranges with the CSS Custom Highlight API, so a search cannot dirty, autosave or enter the undo stack.
Any scripted edit to note content must call history.push() first. Chromium's undo stack cannot see scripted DOM edits, and insertHTML is not the way round it - it rewrites surrounding spaces as  .
The app draws its own menu bar (app-menu.js) and Menu.setApplicationMenu(null) removes Electron's. The menu definitions are the only source the Ctrl+K palette reads.
Toolbar controls that take focus (input, select) clear the editor's selection; field-driven actions must restore it via withSelection or they silently do nothing.
Imported files are sanitised in import.js before they reach the store - a note is loaded with innerHTML and mirrored to disk.
Note export goes through export.js (pure functions) and printToPDF; window.print() only prints, and the print stylesheet must hide all app chrome.
Controls written into a note's markup (the code block's delete button) must be topped up on every paint, or notes written before the control existed never get it.
A fix that lives in a note's markup reaches no note saved before it. src/js/migrate.js runs on every note open and is the only place that class of fix belongs.
An inline span must never wrap a block: text-decoration does not reach a block child, and the span becomes what 'the block the caret is in' resolves to. Wrap one span per block.
Chromium fills a page's margin band with the view's base background colour and paints no CSS background into it, so an export shows the window's backgroundColor there.
A bug reported against a real note must be reproduced with that note's own markup, read out of Nebula-data/storage/notes — a lookalike hid the code-block delete bug through two releases.
The block the caret is in is NOT the editor's direct child: a colour or font wraps a run in a div, so neighbour lookups find the nearest block and step outward.
app.getVersion() returns ELECTRON's version whenever Electron was started against a directory with no package.json (every dev run, every smoke launch).
Every release needs an entry in src/js/release-notes.js; npm run push refuses to ship without one.
A page's margin band cannot be painted from the app: Chromium fills it from a cached document background colour. Use @page { margin: 0 } and pad the content.
cmd() must not call editorEl.focus() when the caret is already inside the editor — a shape's text is a nested editable and focusing the editor discards the selection.
styleWithCSS is a sticky, document-wide flag; applyFont leaves it on, so reset it before any other execCommand.

macOS: identity is null, no custom after-pack signing hook exists, and the build is not Developer ID signed/notarized. The updater explicitly gates automatic installation to win32. Never promise a warning proves safety or cannot recur.
printToPDF needs preferCSSPageSize: true, or Chromium rounds the page box and leaves a sub-point strip of the document background along the top of every page.
execCommand('insertText', '\n') is discarded in a contenteditable; insert the newline as a text node and double it at the end of a block.
::marker is right-aligned in list-style-position: outside — a bullet and a number start at different x however well the text aligns. Draw markers as ::before in a fixed column.
The PDF export is printed from a hidden window loading a standalone white document; only that gives real @page margins on every page.
Every delete key must refuse when a .shape-layer is what would go — Chromium removes a non-editable island whole.
memory.currentPhase is what the docs site prints as 'Right now'; the release fails if it does not name the shipping version.
A <webview> is a separate view: the host stops receiving mousemove/mouseup once the pointer crosses into it. Drag with pointer capture plus a pointer-events shield.
A block whose text is empty but which still holds formatting wrappers is not blank: the caret hides in a few-pixel stub and typing inherits the style. migrateBlankLines clears it.
Shape outline geometry must be in px, not %, or it scales with the shape.
A shape is absolutely positioned: clamp a drag to the note's own extent, measured before the drag, or the scroll height follows the shape.
Guard deletions in beforeinput using getTargetRanges(), not in keydown: Chromium selects a non-editable island on the first Backspace and removes it on the second.
range.intersectsNode cannot see a void element such as <hr> beside a boundary; read the boundary instead.
Toolbar state marks read the DOM at the caret; queryCommandState reports the typing state and carries across a boundary.
A declared 1.6px border is rounded to a whole pixel and an SVG stroke is not — declare the same used width on both or the lines differ.
Never set min-height on a scrolling element: it stops overflowing, stops scrolling, and its scrollTop goes to zero.
execCommand's list commands leave the list inside the caret's own block; normalizeLists lifts it out of any wrapper that is not an <li>.
Drive the real app with a pointer in the order a person works — a clean-start trace can pass while the real sequence fails.
A control that needs a selection must handle the collapsed caret too, or an inherited mark can never be switched off on a new line.
Assert that a label renders at a real width, not merely that its text is in the markup.
